resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1894 Board report gives the tower as 100 feet on a 50-foot bluff; State Parks gives 115 feet to the top of the tower and 100 feet to the focal plane above ground. Different measurements, not a true disagreement.

notes_for_editor: Thin on primary material: the corpus holds Light-House Board reports only from 1891 onward, so 1870s-80s events rest on State Parks and Lighthouse Friends (facts only, own words). Lighthouse Friends material (1878 child death, 1933 fire, 1943 radio beacon, 1960-2011 chronology) is second-hand; the 1878 death is attributed there to the Daily Alta California, which was not read. Source 7 is the same page as 2. The 1914 Bulletin text is a two-column OCR with interleaved columns; the August 1914 rescue quotes were matched line by line and the year taken from the 1914 volume and the 1912-17 index (p. 132). Printed page numbers of the 1894 report are unconfirmed so scan pages are cited. The 987-hour fog-signal figure is from the item numbered 880 in the 1894 report (scan p. 546); the 698-hour figure is the one the same report ties to the fiscal year ended 30 June 1893. The 1896-97 volume covers two reports and the story does not say which year the tank was installed. The roster is from USLHS (cite 10), copied as printed; I did not attempt to connect any person to another station. NRIS 77000337 and Lighthouse Friends say 1977 (an earlier note of 1976 from the Coastside page was not found on recheck). State Parks gives the ship's length as 175 ft, NOAA 162 ft (omitted). Patterson (first assistant 1871-72) and George F. Patterson (second assistant 1872) share a surname; no source says they were related. 'Well over a hundred' people: 147 distinct names in the USLHS roster including Coast Guard crew.
